Fixed. The bug in `stats.js`: `median` always returned `sorted[mid]`, which is only the median for odd-length lists. Even-length lists need the average of the two middle values:

```js
return sorted.length % 2 ? sorted[mid] : (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2;
```

The bug in `stats.js`: `median` returned `sorted[mid]` unconditionally, so even-length lists got the upper middle value instead of the average. It now averages the two middle values when the length is even:

```js

return sorted.length % 2 === 0
  ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2
  : sorted[mid];
```

```js
function median(values) {
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
  return sorted.length % 2 === 0

    : sorted[mid];
}
```

```js
function median(values) {
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
  return sorted.length % 2 === 0
    ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2
    : sorted[mid];
}
```

The current code, for reference:

```js
function median(values) {
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
  return sorted.length % 2 === 0
    ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2
    : sorted[mid];
}
```

The current code, for reference:

```js
function median(values) {
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
  return sorted.length % 2 === 0
    ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2
    : sorted[mid];
}
```

The current code, for reference:

```js
function median(values) {
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
  return sorted.length % 2 === 0
    ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2
    : sorted[mid];
}
```

The current code, for reference:

```js
function median(values) {
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2);
  return sorted.length % 2 === 0
    ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2
    : sorted[mid];
}
```
